name: GitLab
summary: Composio integrates with GitLab using OAuth2 for secure delegated access. The integration allows automated actions such as creating issues, managing repositories, and accessing user profile data. You need to register a user-owned OAuth application in GitLab, configure its credentials in Composio, and select only the necessary scopes for your integration. This setup provides access to GitLab APIs within Composio's automation and AI agent ecosystems.
decision: To set up OAuth with GitLab for use in Composio, you need to register your own OAuth application in your GitLab account (user-owned app), configure the redirect URI as https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/auth-apps/add, copy the client ID and secret, and enter these details into Composio's dashboard along with the same redirect URI and selected scopes. The steps must be performed by a user with access to the relevant GitLab account. Managed setup is not documented.

prerequisites.title: GitLab Account
prerequisites.body: You must have a GitLab account. Sign up for free at gitlab.com if you do not have one.

prerequisites.title: Composio Account
prerequisites.body: You need access to the Composio dashboard to configure OAuth credentials.

steps.title: Sign in to GitLab
steps.body: Go to gitlab.com and sign in with your account.

steps.title: Navigate to Applications
steps.body: Click your profile avatar, choose 'Edit profile', then select 'Applications' from the left sidebar.

steps.title: Create New OAuth Application
steps.body: Click 'New Application', set a name (e.g., Composio GitLab Integration), and enter the redirect URI exactly as: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/auth-apps/add
steps.note: Do not include a trailing slash; must match Composio's setting.

steps.title: Select OAuth Scopes
steps.body: Select scopes per your needs. Examples: read_user, api, read_api. For writing to repos, add write_repository. Only include necessary scopes.

steps.title: Save Application and Copy Credentials
steps.body: Click 'Save application'. Copy the Application ID (Client ID) and Secret (Client Secret).
steps.note: Secret is only shown once on GitLab.

steps.title: Open Composio Dashboard
steps.body: Log in at https://platform.composio.dev/, and create new Auth Config for GitLab.

steps.title: Configure OAuth Details in Composio
steps.body: Enter the Client ID, Client Secret, and redirect URI (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/auth-apps/add) exactly as on GitLab, and specify the same scopes.

steps.title: Complete Connection
steps.body: Use the Connect Account button in Composio’s Auth Config. When prompted, log in to GitLab and approve requested permissions.
steps.note: The consent screen appears; click Authorise.

steps.title: Verify Connection
steps.body: Composio stores the access token once you authorise and connect.

human_actions.title: Register app in GitLab
human_actions.body: Manually register the OAuth application and choose required scopes in your GitLab account.

human_actions.title: Copy/paste client credentials
human_actions.body: Manually copy the Client ID and Secret from GitLab into Composio’s dashboard.

human_actions.title: Authorize access
human_actions.body: Manually approve the application in GitLab when prompted through Composio.
